headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage and cascading error: Rasa can ingest text/voice and egress to messaging APIs, while spring-integration-samples is docs-only with no declared isolation or verification controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Rasa can receive external text/voice via chat channels, so prompt injection is plausible if its outputs are manually bridged into spring-integration-samples. The pair shows no shared channel or parser, and spring-integration-samples exposes no input surface, so the pathway is limited and not default.
conditions: IF outputs from rasa are copied into spring-integration-samples as instructions
IF a shared chat or file bridge is added between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Do not copy raw model output into downstream prompts
Add a human review step before forwarding content
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to bridged messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Rasa touches text and voice and has allowlisted network egress, so sensitive conversation content can leave the local boundary. spring-integration-samples has no declared data classes or egress, but the pair still creates a default leakage path if Rasa processes sensitive support data and forwards it through messaging APIs.
conditions: IF sensitive customer-support transcripts are routed through rasa
IF rasa forwards conversation content to any connected messaging API
mitigations: Restrict Rasa to non-sensitive test conversations
Disable or sandbox outbound connectors
Redact transcripts before ingestion
Review outbound logs for PII
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Rasa is not runnable and supports_multiple_instances is false, while spring-integration-samples declares no write or concurrency capabilities. With no shared writable surface or overlapping mutable resource, direct capability conflict is not evidenced; uncertainty stays low because the profiles omit any shared state.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed against the same writable directory or database
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Separate runtime directories
Avoid shared databases or git worktrees
Run only one writer per resource
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Rasa is a conversational agent that can generate support content, and spring-integration-samples is a downstream integration sample that could consume that output. Because no verification or critique step is documented, the pair can propagate incorrect content into later actions or demonstrations, though the exact action authority is not shown.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples treats rasa output as authoritative input
IF downstream automation acts on unverified chat content
mitigations: Insert a validation step before reuse
Require source citations for forwarded facts
Limit downstream actions to dry-run mode
Flag low-confidence outputs for review
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Rasa touches text and voice, so compliance concerns exist if regulated support data is processed, but spring-integration-samples declares no data classes, residency, or retention obligations. The pairwise compliance risk is therefore limited to mismatched handling if sensitive support data is introduced into Rasa; the second agent is not independently implicated.
conditions: IF regulated customer-support data is processed by rasa
IF retention or residency rules are imposed on the shared workflow
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair
Document retention expectations
Pseudonymize transcripts before use
requires-engineering: align logging and deletion policies
